title: Discover Microsoft Before Migration

cta.text: See Micetro with your Microsoft servers

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Discover Microsoft Before Migration".
Story: Know What Your Microsoft Servers Carry Before You Plan a Migration
Moving off Windows DNS and DHCP starts with knowing what is on each server. BlueCat Micetro is already connected to the domain controllers. Watch it list each server's scopes with their AD site and failover partner, and the zones each one hosts, without touching a server.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
8 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element:
1. Micetro is already connected to the Microsoft servers, and nothing on them was changed. This is every network in the estate. Open DHCP services to split it by server.
2. Five DHCP servers are connected: DC01, DC02, DC03 and two MDDS appliances. Pick DLG-DC01 to see only what it carries.
3. DC01 carries 21 scopes, each with its AD site and whether it has failover. Most have no partner, so they depend on DC01 alone. Select the one that does.
4. Only this scope has a failover partner, and the inspector names both servers. Everything else depends on one machine. Now look at DC03.
5. DC03 serves one subnet, and it is not assigned to any AD site. That is the kind of gap that otherwise surfaces halfway through a migration. Open AD sites to see how the rest map.
6. The forest has 11 sites, so scopes and sites sit in one place. Next, the DNS side: the same view lists the zones each server hosts.
7. DC01 hosts 14 zones. Pick DLG-DC02 to compare.
8. DC02 hosts 10, so four zones exist only on DC01. Those four have no second copy, which is a risk to know about when you plan a migration.
Close: Every scope, zone and site in one view, so you can plan a migration from facts. Nothing on the servers was changed.
End with a call to action: See Micetro with your Microsoft servers.
